Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 21
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Latin American
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Animator
  trauma_type: Witnessed domestic violence (childhood)
  pcl5: 39

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Object Throwing: Throwing objects, Visual (Photos): Related photos, Auditory (Sounds): Related sounds
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Future Plans: Making any plans for the future, Restrict Eating: control eating strictly to feel in control, Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
  Threat: Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively, Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard
  Memory: More Real Than Normal: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things, Olfactory Recall: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened., Blocked Before Complete: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it
  Negative Appraisals: Low Coping: I can't deal with even the slightest upset, No Accountability: The people responsible have faced no consequences, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Luz had grown up in a world of vibrant colors and dynamic movement, but her childhood was also marked by the dark hues of domestic violence. She remembered the sounds of shattering glass, the feeling of crouching behind the couch as objects were thrown across the room. Her mother's cries still echoed in her mind, and the smell of spilled liquor transported her back to those terrifying moments. As she grew older, Luz learned to navigate this treacherous landscape by avoiding anything that might trigger a flashback or a panic attack. She became an expert at sidestepping reminders of her past, steering clear of photos or videos that might show scenes of domestic violence. Even the sound of raised voices or shattering glass made her jump, as if she were still crouched behind that couch, waiting for the storm to pass. Luz's world had shrunk to a tiny, manageable size. She avoided making plans for the future, fearing that something would go terribly wrong and she'd be powerless to stop it. Her strict control over her eating habits was one of the few things that made her feel like she still had some agency in her life. If she could just stick to her diet, maybe she could keep the rest of her world from spinning out of control. As an animator, Luz spent most of her days hunched over a computer screen, lost in a world of fantasy and adventure. But even in this creative haven, reminders of her past lurked. A coworker's raised voice or a careless movement nearby would send her heart racing, as if she were back in that childhood nightmare. She'd try to shake off the feeling, telling herself it was just a minor setback, but deep down, Luz knew she wasn't coping. Her memories of those traumatic events felt more real than any other recollection from her past. They lingered on the edge of her consciousness, waiting to pounce whenever she let her guard down. Sometimes, when she thought about those moments, the smell of spilled liquor or fresh paint would waft up, transporting her back to a time and place she desperately wanted to forget. Luz couldn't shake the feeling that she was trapped in this never-ending cycle of fear and hypervigilance. She felt like she was walking on eggshells, waiting for the next explosion or outburst. Her irritability had become legendary among her friends and family, who tiptoed around her, unsure of what might trigger another angry outburst. One thing that still haunted Luz was the knowledge that no one had ever faced consequences for the harm they'd inflicted on her family. That sense of impunity weighed heavily on her mind, fueling her feelings of helplessness. She couldn't stop bad things from happening to her or those she loved, and this realization left her feeling like a small boat adrift in a stormy sea. Lately, Luz had begun to feel the weight of these unspoken fears bearing down on her. Her relationships were suffering, and even her work was starting to suffer as she found herself unable to focus on anything except her own anxiety. It was then that she realized she needed help – not just for her sake, but for those around her who deserved better than a partner or friend forever stuck in this dark cycle of fear. For the first time in years, Luz began to contemplate seeking professional help. She knew it wouldn't be easy, but something inside her whispered that maybe, just maybe, she didn't have to live like this anymore. Maybe there was a way out of this never-ending nightmare, and all she had to do was take that first step towards healing.
